articles.title: LoP Ritabrata Banerjee files counter complaint against Mamata-Trinamool for fabrication of signature on affidavits
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Leader of Opposition in West Bengal Ritabrata Banerjee on Monday (November 23, 2026) filed a police complaint against Mamata-All India Trinamool Congress for fabricating signatures on affidavits to claim their stake in the party name and symbol. A day earlier, Mamata-Trinamool filed a complaint against Mr. Ritabrata Banerjee under similar allegations.
The Democratic Trinamool Congress MLA, along with Opposition chief whip Akhruzamman and spokesperson Riju Dutta went to the Kalighat Police Station to file the complaint.

“They have threatened many people to sign affidavits; they also manipulated a few MLAs to sign under false pretense. We have already filed complaints at various police stations. We will share them with the ECI,” Mr Ritabrata Banerjee said. He also added that people have been made to sign affidavits under false claims of filling up forms for various schemes, relief materials, and other things and that it was an attempt to “mislead” people.

Since the regime change in West Bengal, the Trinamool Congress has bifurcated into two factions, with almost 65 of 80 Trinamool MLAs rallying behind Mr Ritabrata Banerjee and abandoning the Mamata Banerjee faction. As tensions rose, both factions exercised their claims over the party’s name and symbol. However, Election Commission of India (ECI) barred both from using the original “All India Trinamool Congress” name and the party symbol.
Since the split, both factions have submitted an array of affidavits with the ECI in support of each of the faction’s claim over the symbol and party name.

Mamata-Trinamool leader Subhasish Chakraborty had filed the official complaint dated November 20, against Mr Ritabrata Banerjee at the same Kalighat Police Station for falsification, forging signatures of unsuspecting citizens and creation and fabrication of affidavits which have allegedly been filed before the ECI.
In the complaint filed by Mamata-Trinamool, they have also named Nanoor Police Station Officer-in-charge Sanjoy Sarkar, MLA Arup Roy, and several others as co-conspirators in the case.

“The material and evidence presently in my possession disclose that an organised exercise has been undertaken through the machinery of Nanoor Police Station for the preparation of fake affidavits in support of the rival faction, including affidavits purporting to show that ordinary members of the public recognise Arup Roy as the leader of the AITC and do not accept Smt. Mamata Banerjee as its leader,” reads the copy of the police complaint.

This comes after Mamata-AITC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee had earlier on November 5 claimed that he has video evidence of fabricated affidavits being filed out in favour of Mr. Ritabrata Banerjee.

“He says one thing in the morning, another in the evening and something else at night. Answering his questions is a waste of time and energy. I don’t have that much time,” Mr. Ritabrata Banerjee said on Monday (November 23).
West Bengal / All India Trinamool Congress / Election Commission of India

articles.title: Manik Saha says party probing presence of masked men in BJP election rally
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tripura Chief Minister Dr. Manik Saha on Monday (November 23, 2026) reacted to the presence of several masked youths in a BJP election rally in Agartala on Saturday (November 21). He said he had come to know this from newspaper reports and subsequently took up the matter with the party leadership.
“I don’t support this. In fact, our party does not approve such behaviour from our ranks. The party is inquiring into the matter and will follow up,” he told reporters.

Elections to 21 Urban Local Bodies including Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC) are due on November 27. The ruling BJP has already won five of them unopposed as candidates from other parties and independents did not submit nomination papers.

The appearance of several masked men at the BJP’s election rally in Agartala stirred controversy, with CPI(M) and Congress registering complaints to the state election commission. The Congress also lodged a complaint at the West Agartala Police Station.

Secretary of the State Election Commission on Monday (November 23) said they received complaints about the issues and forwarded them to the police headquarters for necessary action. He said the commission would ensure free and peaceful elections.

BJP sources said veteran minister and city campaign in-charge Ratan Lal Nath organised the procession. They said the masked youths were actually party supporters from Mohanpur, north of Agartala, home Assembly constituency of minister Nath.

CPI(M) and Congress, however, claimed the masked men were actually anti-socials who were likely to be engaged in creating trouble and rig the elections. They also complained of the silence of the police in initiating action despite registering complaints.
Tripura / Communist Party of India -Marxist / Indian National Congress / Bharatiya Janata Party

articles.title: Close to realising PM Narendra Modi’s dream for Kashmir, says Kiren Rijiju
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Terming the work of J&K Waqf Board as “the best-performing” in the country, Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs Kiren Rijiju on Monday (November 23, 2026) said the region is close to achieve the dream Prime Minister Narendra Modi has for it.

Recalling his past tours of Kashmir as Minister of State (MOS) Home and as Law Minister, Mr. Rijiju said, “I remember there were no large programmes as we visited frontier districts to meet soldiers and discuss how to realise the dream of PM Modi. I must say we are very close to realising the dream PM Modi had for Kashmir. He set a goal not only for a peaceful region but also to take J&K to new heights,” said Mr. Rijiju, while speaking at the Waqf Day-2026 at the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology in Srinagar.

Mr. Rijiju said Kashmir was moving ahead at a very “fast pace”. “Seeing the situation today, I can say India’s and J&K’s future is bright. People of Kashmir are large hearted. Today, sportsmen across the country wait to participate in the winter games at Gulmarg every year. The concept, besides adventure and water sports, was introduced in 2019,” said Mr. Rijiju.

Earlier in the day, the Union minister inaugurated the construction of Bibi Halima College of Nursing & Medical Technology (BHCNMT), at Kathi Darwaza, Rainawari, Srinagar. He said the alumni of the educational institute included 16 Kashmir University Gold Medalists, the highest among nursing colleges and over 10 international NCLEX qualifiers in the USA and Canada. “Its graduates also constitute around 30% of nursing officers at SKIMS and over 25% of the nursing workforce at Government Medical College-associated hospitals,” he added.

Praising the arrangements and management at the Nursing College and also the works done at the Hazratnal shrine, Mr. Rijiju said, “The space created at Hazratbal for female pilgrims to offer prayers is beautiful and aesthetically pleasing. I congratulate the Chairperson of the Waqf Board, Darakhshan Andrabi, in this regard. It’s the best performing board in the country.”

The Union Minister also highlighted the need to properly utilise and manage over nine lakh Waqf properties across the country. “It could bring significant socio-economic changes in the Muslim community. Poor and disadvantaged members of the Muslim community could benefit considerably if Waqf assets were utilised for their welfare, of which the J&K Waqf Board’s functioning is an example,” said Mr. Rijiju.
He also congratulated Ms. Andrabi and her entire team for “undertaking development initiatives and improving facilities at important religious and public institutions”.

Praising PM Modi for his vision. Mr. Andrabi said, “I became the first woman chairperson in 2022 and the board was constituted. There was no official structure then and the same was put in place. It is paying dividends.”

National Conference (NC) leader and Member of Parliament (MP) Mian Altaf highlighted the role of Mr. Rijiju pertaining to Kashmir. “He [Rijiju] frequently visits Kashmir and has always loved people. He always tried to contribute to Kashmir as he held different ministries. We all dream to have a better Kashmir, even what it was 30 years ago. My sister Ms. Andrabi is doing work that deserves applaud too,” said Mr. Altaf.
Jammu and Kashmir National Conference / national government / Narendra Modi

articles.title: Will bank manager accept Kayalvizhi Alagiri’s apology, asks Madras High Court
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Madras High Court on Monday (November 23, 2026) wanted to know whether a bank manager would be willing to accept an apology from former Union Minister M.K. Alagiri’s daughter Kayalvizhi Alagiri and agree for closure of a criminal case registered against her for allegedly slapping him supposedly due to anger management issues on July 20, 2026.

Justice V. Lakshminarayanan directed the Inspector of Shastri Nagar police station in Adyar, Chennai to make sure that Harsheen Singh, a branch manager with State Bank of India, appears before the court on Tuesday (November 24, 2026) if he is willing to accept the apology and give a quietus to the issue than continuing the prosecution.

The direction was issued during the hearing of a writ petition (criminal) filed by Ms. Alagiri seeking a direction to the police to register a First Information Report (FIR) against the bank manager on the basis of a counter complaint lodged by her on July 25, 2026 accusing him of having subjected her to verbal abuse, aggressive intimidation and public humiliation.

Government Advocate (criminal side) S. Yogaraja Sekar told the judge that Ms. Alagiri was the owner of a commercial building in which the bank branch was functioning. There was a dispute between the landlady and the tenant over the non-functioning of an elevator in the building and a quarrel over that issue had led to a physical assault against the bank manager on July 20, 2026.

The police had intially registered a First Information Report (FIR) against Ms. Alagiri under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita for abusing and assaulting the bank manager. It also completed the investigation and filed a charge sheet before a Metropolitan Magistrate in Chennai. The Magistrate was slated to take up the case for hearing next on December 22, 2026, the law officer said.

In so far as the counter complaint lodged by the landlady against the bank manager was concerned, the Government Advocate said, the police had conducted a preliminary inquiry but did not find any material to substantiate any of the allegations levelled by her. Therefore, the investigating officer had dropped further action and closed her complaint, he added.
On his part, the petitioner’s counsel S.L. Sudarsanam said, his client would apologise, if necessary and in order to give a quietus to the entire issue.

articles.title: Rajasthan women’s varsity signs MoU with BRICS nations for global leadership centre
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Banasthali Vidyapith, a residential women’s university situated in Rajasthan’s Tonk district, on Monday (November 23, 2026) signed a memorandum of understanding with the BRICS nations for establishment of a centre for global women’s leadership. The new centre will work for women’s educational empowerment and leadership development on a global scale.

The MoU was signed on the conclusion of a five-day BRICS women leaders’ summit, organised on the university campus, which focused on promoting women’s leadership, cultural exchanges, and mutual cooperation and innovative research across the 11 BRICS member countries.

Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla , who inaugurated the summit, called upon women leaders to harness their collective leadership, experience and innovative capabilities to address global challenges and shape a “more peaceful, stable and prosperous” world. He also laid emphasis on cooperation among BRICS nations.

Banasthali Vidyapith organised the summit in partnership with Eurasian Women’s Forum, Russia’s Federation Council, Senezh Management Group of Russia and BRICS Youth Alliance. Vice-Chancellor Ina Aditya Shastri said the participants would act as torchbearers for women’s leadership development in their respective countries.

Extensive discussions were held during the summit on developing women’s leadership in the fields of politics, higher education, science and technology, entrepreneurship, administration, and social development. The speakers agreed to formulate future action plans to address the challenges of inequality in opportunities, limited access to financial resources and socio-cultural barriers.

Senezh Management Workshop’s First Vice-Rector Sergey Vladimirovich Bocharov said the BRICS countries had much to learn from India and Banasthali Vidyapith’s model of women’s leadership. He said the new centre would help expand women’s role in civil society and strengthen their decision-making capacity.

articles.title: Proposal for extending scholarship to Sri Lankan students to pursue medical education in Tamil Nadu
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Sri Lankan Deputy High Commission (SLDHC) in Chennai is proposing to strengthen cooperation in medical education in Tamil Nadu, including the possibility of extending scholarships to Sri Lankan students. Sri Lankan Deputy High Commissioner in Chennai Ganesanathan Geathiswaran met Health Minister K.G. Arunraj in this regard recently.

“During the meeting, discussion focused on further strengthening cooperation in the field of medical education, including the possibility of extending scholarships to Sri Lankan students to pursue medical studies in Tamil Nadu under a proposed 50/50 scholarship between the government of Tamil Nadu and the university concerned,” SLDHC said in a social media post.

Mr. Geathiswaran meeting with the Minister last week also explored the potential for establishing student exchange programmes for medical students and postgraduate trainees, including opportunities for clinical rotations, academic exchanges and professional engagement between medical institutions in Sri Lanka and Tamil Nadu, it said.

articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.
Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return.
Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling.

“Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation.
“Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.”
The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23).
The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025.
Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.
The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

Neocloud and data-center companies, which came under sharp selling pressure earlier following Mr. Huang’s abrupt exit, also climbed. CoreWeave rose 21.5%, IREN gained 26.4% and Nebius advanced ⁠23.4%.
The S&P 500 information technology sector jumped 8.9% and led the gains in the benchmark index.

articles.title: Oil and gas production to pick up in 4-5 years as recent measures take effect, Petroleum Ministry says
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The government expects domestic oil and gas production to pick up in the next 4-5 years as several steps taken in the recent past begin to bear fruit in an industry typically characterised by long gestation periods, The Hindu has learnt.
According to an analysis by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas, the current contraction in domestic oil and gas production is due to factors that took place more than a decade ago.

However, since then, the government has taken steps such as increasing drilling and exploration to record levels, changing laws and rules to provide stable terms to explorers, and opening new avenues for exploration.

“The steps taken in the last few years — new acreage, record drilling, deepwater wells and the revival of Mumbai High — will start showing up in production over the next three to four years,” the note asserted. “That is the nature of this sector: the decisions of one decade decide the output of the next.”
The note also argues that now, unlike earlier, the profits of oil and gas companies upstream companies like ONGC and Oil India are being used to fund exploration rather than subsidies.
“Until 2015, ONGC and Oil India were made to fund a large share of the subsidy on diesel, LPG and kerosene, through discounts on the crude they sold to oil marketing companies,” the note said.

According to data with the Ministry, ONGC paid ₹49,421 crore towards this subsidy in 2012-13 against a profit of ₹20,926 crore, and in 2013-14 paid ₹56,384 crore towards this subsidy against a net profit of ₹22,095 crore.

“In both years ONGC gave away more than twice what it earned,” the note said. “Money that should have gone into finding new oil and gas went into keeping retail prices down. This burden was ended from 2015-16. ONGC now keeps its earnings and has sharply raised its spending on exploration.”
According to the latest data on the Index of Core Industries, the oil and gas sectors have contracted continuously for 22 and 28 months, respectively.

“In this sector it takes five to ten years to go from awarding a block to first production,” a note prepared by the Ministry and accessed by The Hindu said. “Output in 2026 is the result of what was, and was not, done a decade ago.

“After the ninth New Exploration Licensing Policy (NELP) round was launched in 2010, no new exploration round was offered until 2016,” it added. “The fields producing today were not replaced by new ones in that period, and the effect is still being felt.”

The Ministry also stated that mature oil and gas fields generally lose 7-8% of their output every year as reservoir pressure falls and that most of India’s current production comes from such fields. On the other hand, new wells, enhanced recovery, and field redevelopment are making up much of the loss.

articles.title: SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank retain D-SIB status; RBI maintains capital requirements
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has retained State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank in its 2026 list of Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs), maintaining their respective positions under the same bucketing structure as in 2025.

Under the RBI’s framework, SBI, placed in Bucket 4, will have to maintain an additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital requirement of 0.80% of its Risk Weighted Assets (RWAs). HDFC Bank, classified under Bucket 2, will have an additional CET1 requirement of 0.40%, while ICICI Bank, placed in Bucket 1, will have to maintain 0.20%.
These additional capital requirements are over and above the Capital Conservation Buffer, strengthening the banks’ ability to absorb financial shocks and contain systemic risks.

The latest classification is based on data collected from banks as of March 31, 2026. Under the D-SIB framework, banks are categorised into different buckets according to their Systemic Importance Scores (SISs), with higher scores attracting higher additional capital requirements.

The RBI introduced the Framework for Dealing with D-SIBs on July 22, 2014, subsequently updating it on December 28, 2023. The framework requires the central bank to publicly disclose the names of designated D-SIBs annually, beginning in 2015, and assign them to appropriate buckets based on their systemic importance.

SBI and ICICI Bank were initially designated as D-SIBs in 2015 and 2016, respectively. HDFC Bank joined the list in 2017, when all three banks were identified as systemically important financial institutions.

articles.title: Core accountability: On core sector performance
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

articles.title: Rampur’s Lavi Fair: Storytelling through 300 years of Himalayan trade and tradition
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: What Disneyland is to children today, Lavi Fair in Rampur Bushahr, in Himachal Pradesh’s Shimla district, was to my family in the 1980s. I recall wandering through the fair as an eight-year-old, watching an old man smoking a chillum beside heaps of black sheep fleece and stacks of white woollen pattus (traditional garments of Kinnaur and Kullu women).

Mother and her friends carefully chose shawls for their daughters’ and future daughters-in-law’s trousseaux. Years later, I received a beautiful black sheep wool and pashmina shawl for my wedding. Wool finds pride of place at the fair. The name Lavi is linked to “Loe”, a sheet of woollen cloth and the practice of shearing sheep.

articles.title: Must balance ‘economic patriotism’ with cultural heritage: GJC on PM Modi’s call to stop gold purchases
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: While welcoming Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s call for prioritising locally-made products and reducing gold imports, the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) has said that India must balance “economic patriotism” and its cultural traditions when it comes to gold jewellery.

It argued that the sector contributes “nearly 7-8%” to the economy and supports “millions of livelihoods”. The GJC was reacting to Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s recent and repeated appeal to all Indians to stop foreign trips and weddings, to buy local, and to only buy gold if necessary.

“The Prime Minister’s appeal for economic patriotism and greater preference for Swadeshi products is timely and welcome,” Rajesh Rokde, Chairman of the All India Gem & Jewellery Domestic Council (GJC) said.

“While we fully support the Prime Minister’s call for restraint when gold is viewed purely as bullion or an investment instrument, jewellery consumption remains closely linked to culture, craftsmanship, and livelihoods,” Mr. Rokde added.
He said that gold and jewellery hold a unique place in India’s cultural heritage, particularly during festive and wedding seasons, such as the period that India will soon enter in October-December.
“The jewellery industry, contributing nearly 7-8% to the economy and supporting millions of livelihoods, is an integral part of India’s growth story,” Mr. Rokde asserted.
‘People bought less gold, prices fell’: Modi recalls year-old appeal

“As a ₹10 lakh crore industry, the Indian jewellery sector must continue to grow responsibly, with greater transparency, value creation, and alignment with national priorities — balancing economic patriotism with India’s enduring cultural traditions,” he added.

articles.title: Chinese neuroscientist at Princeton is held by ICE after detention at Washington airport
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A Chinese neuroscience researcher at Princeton University is in the custody of immigration authorities after she was detained while trying to get on a flight back from Washington, marking another instance of federal enforcement at airports.

Eva Yi Xie, a third-year doctoral student at Princeton, was detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport on Thursday (November 19, 2026) as she tried to fly back to New Jersey from a conference in the nation's capital, her university adviser Carlos Brody said in a social media post.
The Department of Homeland Security, which oversees ICE, says Ms. Xie overstayed her visa and did not have authorisation to study in the United States.

“News of Eva's detention is distressing for me and many members of the Princeton University community,” Rodney Priestley, dean of the university's graduate school, said in a statement. "We hope Eva will soon be able to resume her studies at Princeton.”

Two days after Ms. Xie was taken into custody in Washington, masked immigration officers detained a father and daughter on an airport jet bridge in Seattle. ICE has ramped up detentions at airports since the summer, especially targeting people it says have overstayed their visas.

Kerry Doyle, Ms. Xie's lawyer, said she came to the U.S. at age 14 with her family from China and has had an asylum application pending for years. Mr. Doyle insisted that Ms. Xie has permission to live, work and study in the U.S. while her case is pending.
Mr. Doyle said Ms. Xie is being held in ICE's Caroline Detention Centre in Virginia.

DHS said in a statement that Ms. Xie came to the United States on a temporary visa on March 16, 2016, but “chose to violate our nation's laws by refusing to depart by the required date of September 15, 2016.”
The agency said she did not have valid permission to study in the U.S. and “a pending application does not confer legal status.”
“Xie will receive due process and remain in ICE custody pending her removal proceedings," the DHS statement said.

Democratic Senator Cory Booker of New Jersey said in a statement that his office contacted ICE and didn't get a “satisfactory response” about why she was detained. New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill, also a Democrat, directed her administration to coordinate with federal lawmakers and the state of Virginia to get more information.

“While ICE claims to go after the worst of the worst, time and again the record shows they do not -- and their tactics are making New Jerseyans less safe,” Ms. Sherrill's spokesperson, Steve Sigmund, said in an email.

articles.title: Federal appeals court gives President Donald Trump path to erasing hush money conviction
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: A federal appeals court on Monday (November 23, 2026) gave U.S. President Donald Trump a new pathway to erasing his hush money criminal conviction, moving the case to a federal court where he could seek to have it dismissed on immunity grounds.

A three-judge panel of the 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals reversed a lower court decision that had kept the case in state court in New York, where Mr. Trump was tried and convicted on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records to obscure a $130,000 payment to adult film performer Stormy Daniels.

The panel ordered a lower court to promptly issue a decision on whether the case should remain in federal court. If that happens, Mr. Trump could then argue that the verdict should be discarded because of Presidential immunity.

The decision also set in motion a halt to proceedings in Mr. Trump's simultaneous state court appeal. Trump denies wrongdoing and was given no punishment in the case, which made him the first U.S. President convicted of a crime.

In a two-page order, the 2nd Circuit panel said it disagreed with the late US District Judge Alvin Hellerstein's earlier denial of Mr. Trump's request to move the historic case from state court to federal court, a process known as removal.

articles.title: A framework for nuclear risk reduction cannot wait
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: For the first time since 1972, there is no treaty formally restricting the world’s largest nuclear arsenals. New START (New Strategic Arms Reduction Treaty) expired in February, and nine months later, a successor treaty is still far from being drafted. Russia had offered to keep observing New START’s limits for a year if the United States did the same. Instead, the U.S. has pushed for an “improved” agreement, insisting that any nuclear treaty must involve China, which understandably has its own reservations.

On November 19, the leaders of the three countries met for the first time on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen. They issued a joint declaration reaffirming that a nuclear war must never be fought. They also pledged subsequent talks on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation. However, there are no provisions for the verification of compliance with these commitments, and no date seems to have been fixed for further talks. Despite Shenzhen, the underlying tension between the three countries’ positions remains. Each country’s position makes sense from where it sits, but at a time fraught with conflict, further complicated by emerging technologies, this treaty-less scenario cannot continue indefinitely.

articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after U.S. government input
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Nvidia on Monday (November 23, 2026) reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior U.S. government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal.
U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.”

The board voted unanimously to bring Mr. Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead”, the company said in a statement.
Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board.

The decision came three days after Mr. Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Mr. Huang back, calling him “one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world” and saying he would “love to see Jensen be given a second chance.”
Mr. Trump described Mr. Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions" and said the company should rehire him “if they were smart".
Mr. Huang had offered to return, but the board initially refused.
Board chair Harvey Jones had said on an earnings call last week that directors had unanimously accepted his resignation and did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".
“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Mr. Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family. “I can’t wait to get back to work.”

Mr. Huang, 63, stepped down on November 12 following reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that bought billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips.
U.S. intelligence services reportedly concluded she passed information to Beijing, which has denied the allegations.

articles.title: Armenia drops Nagorno-Karabakh claim in proposed new constitution
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Armenian leader Nikol Pashinyan unveiled a draft constitution on Monday (November 23, 2026) that would get rid of a 1990 independence clause and claim to the disputed Karabakh region, saying it was the only way to reach a peace deal with Azerbaijan.
The Caucasus foes have been locked in a territorial conflict over the mountainous region since the fall of the Soviet Union.
In a 2023 offensive, Baku retook the Armenian-populated region, forcing a mass exodus, and has since demanded that Yerevan change its constitution for a peace treaty to be possible.
Mr. Pashinyan addressed Armenians, promising a peace treaty with Azerbaijan should his countrymen back the new constitution in a referendum.

Mr. Pashinyan said the new text rejects "the logic of the Declaration of Independence of August 23, 1990 — that is, the logic of conflict" and said the aim of the new constitution is to "ensure peace".

The draft deletes the 1990 preamble, which included a clause for re-unification with the Nagorno-Karabakh region and called for the international recognition of the genocide of Armenians by the Ottoman Empire.
Armenia's Opposition has accused Mr. Pashinyan of bowing to Azerbaijan's demands under pressure, calling it "Aliyev's Constitution" — after Azerbaijani leader Ilham Aliyev.
But Mr. Pashinyan told Armenians not to believe "that we are doing this for someone else under external pressure".
Mr. Pashinyan — whose party is several seats short of a constitutional majority in Parliament — called on the Opposition not to block the referendum.
"If the people will vote against the constitution, I will resign," he said.
"If they will vote for it, then I will not run for Prime Minister in the next elections," he added.
Mr. Pashinyan, who came to power on the back of mass protests in 2018, has said Armenia's current constitution is linked to the "oligarchy" of previous authoritarian authorities.

articles.title: Fatal disagreement: on the COP31 summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: COP31 ended in Antalya, Türkiye, with a whimper. The 190-odd countries that had convened for nearly 12 days — a close to 50-hour overshoot — failed to agree on an overarching political statement , called a cover text, that acts as a stepping stone to future, collective global action on climate change. Usually, cover texts evolve as a final synthesis of deliberations ; the COP31 leadership, helmed by Türkiye and Australia, thought it fit to push for a cover text early in the proceedings. The headline sought was a global electrification target: 35% of global final energy consumption will come from electricity by 2035, in the hope that this would reduce direct fossil fuel emissions. Ultimately, the cover text failed to pass muster because the European Union objected to the text’s lack of any explicit mention of ‘fossil fuel,’ let alone its phase-out. The COP process is arduously protracted as even a single country’s objection can stall progress. Country-blocks outside the EU, such as coalitions of the least developed countries, island nations, some South American countries — reportedly 130 countries — were also insistent on fossil fuel language. While COP 31 made some progress on old pathways, such as the Just Transition agreement, it is perplexing that the delegations could not make progress on the other big prong of negotiations: climate finance.

The increase in solar panel installations and the significant shift towards battery use in grid storage and transport did not come cheap: the cost of the land required for their installation, their intermittent nature of being dependent on weather, grid upgrades all carry costs. It is global markets, imperfectly connected, but connected, that have managed to bring it to this stage over decades. India and China, major fossil emitters, with large, still indigent populations, are also leaders in total clean energy installations. Therefore it stands to reason that developed countries, which have committed to providing climate finance in recognition of their historical emissions, make good on past promises to shoulder the cost of the carbon emissions that are responsible for warming. Economic crises are a feature, and not a bug, of the interconnected financial system enveloping the world and there are, undeniably, challenges to diverting the necessary finance towards countries most vulnerable to climate change impact. However, it is no longer prudent to sweep this under the rug by scuttling experimental approaches — namely carbon capture — as inimical to the broader commitment to eschew fossil fuel. When the primary framework climate agreement was crafted three decades ago, nobody envisaged AI and the drain that data centres portended or the wars that would see the vociferous antagonists of coal immediately shore up their gas reserves. Without honest good-faith dialogue, the COP is at risk of being a sideshow: a mortal blow to multilateralism.

articles.title: Wall Street roars back as Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Wall Street’s main indexes rallied sharply on Monday (November 23, 2026), led by a ​nearly 7% jump in the tech-heavy Nasdaq, as investors rushed back into AI-linked stocks ⁠after Nvidia said it had reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive.
Nvidia shares surged 32.2%, on track for their biggest one-day jump in more than two decades after an extraordinary reversal, which followed President Donald Trump’s call for Mr. Huang’s return.
Mr. Huang resigned ‌as chief executive earlier this month over revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.
The chipmaker is widely regarded as a cornerstone of the AI trade, and ‌its sharp rebound helped lift sentiment across the sector after weeks of heavy selling.

“Huang’s return ‌marks ⁠one of the biggest reversals in the history of the stock market. Never has so ⁠much value rested on the shoulders of a single executive,” said David Russell, global head of market strategy at TradeStation.
“Wall Street envisioned a stock market without his leadership and didn’t like what it saw.”
The Nasdaq-100 was on track to add more than $2 trillion ​in market value on Monday (November 23).
The Nasdaq ‌Composite and the S&P 500 were on track for their biggest one-day gains since markets surged after Mr. Trump paused his “Liberation Day” tariff package in April 2025.
Chip stocks gained, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up 13.4% and also on track for its best session since April 2025.
The rally was broad-based in ‌the tech sphere, with the so-called Magnificent Seven stocks Tesla, Amazon , Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet climbing ​between 5.8% and 12.4%.

Neocloud and data-center companies, which came under sharp selling pressure earlier following Mr. Huang’s abrupt exit, also climbed. CoreWeave rose 21.5%, IREN gained 26.4% and Nebius advanced ⁠23.4%.
The S&P 500 information technology sector jumped 8.9% and led the gains in the benchmark index.

articles.title: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO after U.S. government input
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Nvidia on Monday (November 23, 2026) reinstated Jensen Huang as chief executive after input from senior U.S. government officials left its board confident he posed no national security risk, less than two weeks after the co-founder resigned due to an alleged spy scandal.
U.S. President Donald Trump welcomed the move as a “correct and proper decision.”

The board voted unanimously to bring Mr. Huang back as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately, after a series of meetings left directors satisfied with his “candor and ability to lead”, the company said in a statement.
Nvidia did not name the government officials it consulted or say what they told the board.

The decision came three days after Mr. Trump publicly urged Nvidia to take Mr. Huang back, calling him “one of the truly most brilliant minds in the world” and saying he would “love to see Jensen be given a second chance.”
Mr. Trump described Mr. Huang as “a good man” who “made some bad decisions" and said the company should rehire him “if they were smart".
Mr. Huang had offered to return, but the board initially refused.
Board chair Harvey Jones had said on an earnings call last week that directors had unanimously accepted his resignation and did “not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO".
“I take this responsibility with the greatest humility and renewed commitment,” Mr. Huang said, thanking the board, staff, shareholders and his family. “I can’t wait to get back to work.”

Mr. Huang, 63, stepped down on November 12 following reports that he had a relationship with Alice Huang — no relation — a former executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed, a company that bought billions of dollars’ worth of Nvidia chips.
U.S. intelligence services reportedly concluded she passed information to Beijing, which has denied the allegations.

Board chair Harvey Jones said on Monday (November 23, 2026) that directors now believe Mr. Huang “is the right person to lead Nvidia” and that his return serves the interests of shareholders, employees, partners and customers.

articles.title: India maps landslide susceptibility as part of shift from post-disaster relief to landslide management
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: India has completed a national landslide susceptibility mapping exercise across approximately 4.3 lakh square kilometres, while the landslide inventory database has compiled information on nearly 91,000 historical landslides by the end of 2025, Minister for Science and Technology Jitendra Singh said on Monday (November 23, 2026).

He noted that India is progressively shifting its approach to landslide management, from post-disaster relief to prevention, preparedness, and risk reduction, marking a “major transformation” in the country’s disaster management strategy.

He was speaking at the 7th World Landslide Forum being held at the Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham, Faridabad. This is the first time the periodic International Consortium on Landslides and the International Programme on Landslides is being held in India. The 4-day programme brought together international experts, scientists, and policymakers from more than 75 countries.

Recalling major landslide disasters in Kerala’s Wayanad and Uttarakhand’s Chamoli, as well as in Sikkim, Himachal Pradesh, and Jammu and Kashmir, Dr. Singh stressed the need for interdisciplinary research, continuous monitoring, and coordinated scientific efforts to minimise the impact of such disasters.

The National Landslide Forecasting Centre was established in Kolkata in 2024 and has now extended its activities to 20 districts, according to a statement from the Department of Science and Technology. The Regional Landslide Forecasting System, established in 2020, is supporting experimental and operational forecasting across vulnerable regions, it added.

articles.title: Severe anaemia affects less than 2% of population: ICMR survey
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: According to a survey by the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR), severe anaemia was observed in less than 2% of people in the majority of age groups. The Survey for Assessment of Markers of Population Health, Activity, Diet and Anthropometry (SAMPADA) 2023-2025 was released on Monday (November 23, 2026).

It showed that children aged 12-59 months had 42% anaemia prevalence, adolescent girls aged 10-19 years had anaemia prevalence of 46%, adolescent boys aged 10-19 years and men aged 20–59 years had 22-23% anaemia prevalence, whereas women of reproductive age had 56% prevalence.
The survey also found that mild anaemia constitutes a substantial proportion of the overall anaemia burden.

“SAMPADA provides nationally representative estimates of anaemia across children, adolescents, adults, pregnant and lactating women and older adults, together with detailed information on micronutrient deficiencies to evaluate potential causes of anaemia. It is encouraging that prevalence of anaemia is lower in SAMPADA compared to previous national surveys. The comprehensive anaemia profiling in the SAMPADA survey provides an evidence base to strengthen the ongoing national efforts towards Anaemia Mukt Bharat,” said Rajiv Bahl, secretary, Department of Health Research.

The report noted that about half of anaemic women, including pregnant and lactating women, adolescent girls, and children, have mild anaemia, indicating considerably lower risk of serious health consequences than moderate or severe anaemia. Anaemia prevalence is much lower among adolescent boys, adult and older men, and even among those affected, three-fourths have only mild anaemia, said the release issued by the Union Health Ministry.

SAMPADA represents one of the largest and most comprehensive nutrition surveys undertaken globally. The survey covered more than 2 lakh individuals from over 81,000 households across 183 districts in 35 States and Union Territories. More than 1.7 lakh blood samples were analysed for haemoglobin estimation across different age, sex, and physiological groups.

“A major strength of SAMPADA is the use of gold standard method of venous blood sampling and automated analysers for haemoglobin estimation, providing greater accuracy and reproducibility. In a sub-sample, the survey also assessed iron status, folate, vitamin B12, together with inflammatory biomarkers C-reactive protein (CRP) and alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AGP) to obtain national level prevalence estimates,” the release said.
Iron deficiency accounts for about half of the anaemia cases in women, adolescent girls, and children, said the report.

The micronutrient assessment showed that although iron deficiency is the predominant contributor to anaemia in vulnerable population groups, it accounts for about half of the overall anaemia burden, highlighting the need to simultaneously address multiple nutritional and non-nutritional causes of anaemia, including infections, hemoglobinopathies, and inflammation related to chronic disease.

However, the prevalence of vitamin B12 and folate deficiency was similar in both anaemic and non-anaemic individuals across population groups, indicating a limited contribution of these micronutrient deficiencies to anaemia in India.

Iron deficiency is concentrated in specific life-stages and in moderate and severe cases of anaemia. SAMPADA findings show that iron deficiency is largely restricted to population groups including under-five children, adolescent girls, and women of reproductive age, while adolescent boys, men, and the elderly have a low prevalence of iron deficiency. Importantly, people with moderate and severe anaemia have a high prevalence of iron deficiency and need to be identified by testing for appropriate treatment and tracking till resolution as envisaged in AMB 2.0.

“These findings support more targeted, population-specific and life-course approaches to anaemia prevention and management. The evidence can contribute, while also identifying areas where further research and improved surveillance are required,” said Bharati Kulkarni, director, ICMR-NIN.

articles.title: Rotary Club of Madras partners with Tamil Nadu government to vaccinate 3.5 lakh girls against HPV
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Rotary Club of Madras (RCM) and the Tamil Nadu government have entered into a partnership to provide human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination to 3.5 lakh adolescent girls to prevent cervical cancer.

The partnership, valued at approximately ₹200 crore, is among the largest public-private initiatives for HPV vaccination in India. It was acknowledged in the presence of Darez Ahamed, Secretary, Health and Family Welfare Department, Tamil Nadu government.

High-risk HPV infections account for more than 95% of cervical cancer cases. HPV vaccination during adolescence helps prevent infections caused by high-risk HPV types and reduces the risk of cervical cancer later in life.

Bobby Krishna, president of the Rotary Club of Madras, said the partnership was part of Rotary’s efforts to work with the government on large-scale vaccination programmes. articles.title: Fatal disagreement: on the COP31 summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: COP31 ended in Antalya, Türkiye, with a whimper. The 190-odd countries that had convened for nearly 12 days — a close to 50-hour overshoot — failed to agree on an overarching political statement , called a cover text, that acts as a stepping stone to future, collective global action on climate change. Usually, cover texts evolve as a final synthesis of deliberations ; the COP31 leadership, helmed by Türkiye and Australia, thought it fit to push for a cover text early in the proceedings. The headline sought was a global electrification target: 35% of global final energy consumption will come from electricity by 2035, in the hope that this would reduce direct fossil fuel emissions. Ultimately, the cover text failed to pass muster because the European Union objected to the text’s lack of any explicit mention of ‘fossil fuel,’ let alone its phase-out. The COP process is arduously protracted as even a single country’s objection can stall progress. Country-blocks outside the EU, such as coalitions of the least developed countries, island nations, some South American countries — reportedly 130 countries — were also insistent on fossil fuel language. While COP 31 made some progress on old pathways, such as the Just Transition agreement, it is perplexing that the delegations could not make progress on the other big prong of negotiations: climate finance.

The increase in solar panel installations and the significant shift towards battery use in grid storage and transport did not come cheap: the cost of the land required for their installation, their intermittent nature of being dependent on weather, grid upgrades all carry costs. It is global markets, imperfectly connected, but connected, that have managed to bring it to this stage over decades. India and China, major fossil emitters, with large, still indigent populations, are also leaders in total clean energy installations. Therefore it stands to reason that developed countries, which have committed to providing climate finance in recognition of their historical emissions, make good on past promises to shoulder the cost of the carbon emissions that are responsible for warming. Economic crises are a feature, and not a bug, of the interconnected financial system enveloping the world and there are, undeniably, challenges to diverting the necessary finance towards countries most vulnerable to climate change impact. However, it is no longer prudent to sweep this under the rug by scuttling experimental approaches — namely carbon capture — as inimical to the broader commitment to eschew fossil fuel. When the primary framework climate agreement was crafted three decades ago, nobody envisaged AI and the drain that data centres portended or the wars that would see the vociferous antagonists of coal immediately shore up their gas reserves. Without honest good-faith dialogue, the COP is at risk of being a sideshow: a mortal blow to multilateralism.

articles.title: Just verdict: on Myanmar and the International Court of Justice
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: On November 19, the International Court of Justice held that Myanmar committed genocide against the Rohingya. It is for the first time that the court has found any state responsible for the crime. The verdict, with nine votes to six, was not lightly reached. Genocide requires proof of an intent to destroy a group. In the absence of direct evidence of a plan, the court could infer that intent only if it was “the only reasonable inference” from the facts, a high bar to affix responsibility. The facts it accepted are harrowing. In 2017, in what Myanmar’s army called “clearance operations” against the insurgent Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army, at least 10,000 Rohingya were killed, 1,834 raped and 392 villages destroyed in northern Rakhine State. Over 7,00,000 fled to Bangladesh. Then Army chief Min Aung Hlaing, now Myanmar’s “civilian” President, called the “Bengali problem” an “unfinished job”. Myanmar argued that it had only been fighting insurgents or at worst, driving the Rohingya out or punishing them. The court said that the army drew no distinction between fighters and civilians, had no plan to move anyone, fired on fleeing people and killed children on a scale that could not be explained as punishment. Seen alongside decades of discrimination, the evidence pointed to an intent to destroy.

The incidents of 2017 were no aberration. The army drove lakhs of Rohingya into Bangladesh in 1978 and 1991-92. The junta stripped the Rohingya of citizenship in 1982 and the state branded them as “foreigners” in Arakan, disenfranchising them in 2015. While the junta’s Bamar-Buddhist vision has oppressed every minority, the Rohingya have been subjected to the most brutality. More than 1.2 million are in Bangladesh, living in dilapidated conditions, made worse due to diminished international aid. The court ordered Myanmar to allow their safe, voluntary and dignified return and to compensate them, but it has no means of enforcing its judgment. Only the UN Security Council can, but it will be subject to vetoes by Myanmar’s backers, China and Russia. On the very day of the verdict, the two joined the U.S. in Shenzhen to declare the “immunities of State officials” of “paramount importance”. Others, India among them, have courted the regime in Naypyitaw regardless, following sham elections that made the junta leader civilian President earlier this year. And Rakhine State, mired in civil war, is now mostly held by the Arakan Army which is accused of atrocities against the Rohingya. Only a truly democratic, federal, plural and peaceful Myanmar can bring the Rohingya home in safety.

articles.title: Core accountability: On core sector performance
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The core sector performance in October is a good example of how statistical distortions can create incorrect assessments of the economy. The 10.9% growth rate, a series high, has been celebrated as a sign of the Indian economy’s strength and resilience. There is, no doubt, an aspect of this has been reflected in the numbers, especially to do with infrastructure creation. However, the much more impactful factor behind the high core sector growth was a low base effect. The overall Index of Core Industries grew just 0.8% in October 2025 and so, in relation, the performance in October 2026 looked that much faster. This low base effect is even starker when looking at individual sectors within the index. The coal sector grew at a blistering 23% in October, more than twice its growth rate in the previous month. Yet, a large part of this was propelled by the fact that the sector had contracted nearly 8.5% last October. The rest of the sector’s growth was driven by demand of the electricity and iron ore sectors, or so the data show. The electricity sector also grew at a series high of nearly 22% in October, but on the back of a near-7% contraction in October last year. This base effect anomaly is likely down to the fact that the festive season starts at different but similar points every year. As such, a more accurate reading of the economy will be possible once the data for November are available.

The construction-related sectors seem to have seen genuine growth, a reflection of the government’s ongoing infrastructure push. The iron ore sector’s growth rate accelerated to a three-month high of 26.4% in October 2026 as compared to a growth of 8.7% in the same month last year. Steel grew at 7.3% versus 9.5% last year, and cement by 15.4% versus 5.2%. The economy’s dependence on government spending is not going to ease in the near future, and might even intensify as higher costs eat into companies’ profit margins. The core sector data once again highlighted a major reason for these higher costs — the oil and gas sectors. The crude oil sector shrank by 4.1%, its 22nd consecutive month of contraction. The natural gas sector, similarly, contracted 7.6%, a series-worst performance and the 28th straight month of contraction. A major reason behind high inflation in India is the underperformance of these two sectors and the resultant dependence on imported fuel. It is time the Petroleum Ministry candidly explains — to Parliament in December or to the public directly — why India’s fuel output has been continuously falling. If it is a matter of a lack of resources underground, that is one thing, but the underperformance of oil and gas public sector undertakings is quite another. Accountability needs to be set.

articles.title: Paper tiger: On the Green India Mission
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: That all was not well with the Green India Mission was clear even before its approval. After the UPA-I government announced it in 2008, the Ministry of Rural Development had objected to its financial design much before the Union Cabinet approved it in 2014. But the Environment Ministry proceeded anyway and retained largely the same arrangement when it revised the Mission in 2021. Following the Comptroller and Auditor General’s report, on November 19, the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) upbraided the Ministry for the Mission’s virtual failure and for still not having issued the implementation guidelines for the revised form. The original 10-year vision was to expand forest and tree cover by 5 million hectares (mha), improve forest quality on another 5 mha, improve forest-related livelihoods for 3 million households, and sequester up to 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. The outlay was ₹46,000 crore. In 2014, the Cabinet approved ₹13,000 crore for 1.4 mha each of the first two objectives by 2018, but to be supported to the tune of 81.5% by Compensatory Afforestation Fund Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA), National Afforestation Programme (NAP), and MGNREGS funds. In 2021-22, the Ministry folded the NAP into the Mission and, in mid-2025, unveiled a revised version with an allocation of ₹12,190 crore to improve forest cover on 25 mha by 2030, including 24 mha through other schemes. The government had thus expanded the primary target but left the Mission responsible for only 1 mha.

Together with the CAMPA, NAP, and MGNREGS funds never materialising, it is no surprise that the programmes to improve forest quality and forest cover have respectively fallen short by 91.8% and 97.5% vis-à-vis the 2014 target. The Environment Ministry had assembled a large programme around resources that it knew it could not control. Pro-climate work in practice ought to span government schemes to deliver action and justice, and the Ministry ought to have formalised the division of responsibilities and accounting system. The PAC’s new demand that the Ministry submit an implementation timetable is insufficient. From the Jal Shakti Abhiyan in 2019 to the Dharti Aaba Janjatiya Gram Utkarsh Abhiyan in 2024, the government has often floated new programmes banking significantly on funds from existing schemes — an untenable policy when the latter also have their own obligations. And if the VB-G RAM G scheme was to also advance climate justice, the government should not have undermined the erstwhile demand-driven funding model and shifted more financial responsibility to the States. Climate action has to be timely, for which the Union government must dedicate adequate resources and proactively ensure that its initiatives are implemented.

articles.title: Going public on AI: On Anthropic IPO
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The Initial Public Offering (IPO) of Anthropic , PBC is a mile marker in the arms race to develop superintelligent systems driven by generative AI . Traders valued the firm at $1.27 trillion, a denomination that is bound to become more and more familiar in an industry backed by an endless appetite for capital and unprecedented forms of financialisation. Anthropic’s statements emphasise warnings on the safety of its systems and the consequences of unbridled development of advanced systems. In the history of the development of this technology, this PR spin may just be a blip. After all, their testing has led to AI agents that have broken out of sandboxes and infected unsuspecting organisations’ internal systems: a deluge of agentic chaos that is already a reality has led to little signs of the firm backing its words with action. A familiar trend is playing out, with open source LLMs showing frontier capabilities that can back their erratic impulses, appearing in the space of just months, or sometimes weeks. Advocates of pacing the frontier and managing these emerging risks have been marginalised in a way that has little precedent in this century. It is time for governments to get involved, and specifically, for India to raise its voice on these risks, loudly and unequivocally.

While India’s AI industry is nascent, its positions on international forums carry the weight of a sixth of humanity. A mix of cynical calculations and practical considerations have blunted the use of that voice, for example in the U.S.’s hugely destabilising war of choice against Iran, and Israel’s ongoing genocide in Gaza. In taking a strong position on what could be the defining transformation of this decade, India has little to lose, and a lot to contribute. Out-of-control AI agents promise, moreover, significant disruption to outdated government and private systems online. While India has little commercial leverage to curb San Francisco’s accelerationism, its voice is sure to be noticed. India cannot be silent amid a U.S.-China technological race which could lead to catastrophic damage. New Delhi must not allow the U.S. to stop it from pushing for AI safety.

articles.title: Three to tango: On Trump, Xi, Putin trilateral summit
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The first trilateral summit between the Presidents of China, the U.S. and Russia , held in Shenzhen on November 19, reflected both the changing global order and the leaders’ shared desire to remain engaged with one another in an increasingly unpredictable world. For U.S. President Donald Trump, the summit was a platform where he could push for joint talks between the world’s three largest nuclear powers on reducing nuclear warheads. After the New START treaty between the U.S. and Russia expired in February 2026, Moscow had signalled that it was ready for talks, but Mr. Trump wanted to involve China as well. For President Xi Jinping, the summit reinforced China’s position as a peer competitor to the U.S. While Russia seeks to deepen partnership with China, the U.S. is looking to build strategic stability. And for Russian President Vladimir Putin, whom the West sought to isolate after he launched the invasion of Ukraine, the summit offered a seat at the high table. The decision to start trilateral talks on nuclear arms and the joint declaration, which stated that ‘a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought’, are steps in the right direction. But much will depend on what follows.

Many had compared the meet to the 1945 Yalta Conference, when Russian leader Joseph Stalin, U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt and British Prime Minister Winston Churchill met to discuss the future of post-War Europe. But Shenzhen was not a summit of the victors of a major war. This was more about three great powers setting terms of engagement in a changing world. The summit failed to achieve any breakthrough on any of the issues on the agenda — nuclear arms reduction, non-proliferation or the Ukraine war — or even offer a road map for the future. Moreover, it is not clear if the Shenzhen spirit could be sustained in the medium to long-term as another President in the U.S. could take a very different approach towards Russia and China. The three leaders have called for reform of the UN. While it is a welcome move, any attempt to reform the international system and institutions must also involve other powers, particularly rising middle powers such as India, South Africa and Brazil. But the Shenzhen framework could bring greater stability and predictability to great-power relations. This is important given that two of the Big Three are currently waging two separate wars. The leaders should draw up a clear road map for nuclear talks and other key issues outlined in the Shenzhen declaration, with realistic and achievable objectives. Otherwise, the summit would amount to little more than another diplomatic photo-op.

articles.title: LoP Ritabrata Banerjee files counter complaint against Mamata-Trinamool for fabrication of signature on affidavits
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Leader of Opposition in West Bengal Ritabrata Banerjee on Monday (November 23, 2026) filed a police complaint against Mamata-All India Trinamool Congress for fabricating signatures on affidavits to claim their stake in the party name and symbol. A day earlier, Mamata-Trinamool filed a complaint against Mr. Ritabrata Banerjee under similar allegations.
The Democratic Trinamool Congress MLA, along with Opposition chief whip Akhruzamman and spokesperson Riju Dutta went to the Kalighat Police Station to file the complaint.

“They have threatened many people to sign affidavits; they also manipulated a few MLAs to sign under false pretense. We have already filed complaints at various police stations. We will share them with the ECI,” Mr Ritabrata Banerjee said. He also added that people have been made to sign affidavits under false claims of filling up forms for various schemes, relief materials, and other things and that it was an attempt to “mislead” people.

Since the regime change in West Bengal, the Trinamool Congress has bifurcated into two factions, with almost 65 of 80 Trinamool MLAs rallying behind Mr Ritabrata Banerjee and abandoning the Mamata Banerjee faction. As tensions rose, both factions exercised their claims over the party’s name and symbol. However, Election Commission of India (ECI) barred both from using the original “All India Trinamool Congress” name and the party symbol.
Since the split, both factions have submitted an array of affidavits with the ECI in support of each of the faction’s claim over the symbol and party name.

Mamata-Trinamool leader Subhasish Chakraborty had filed the official complaint dated November 20, against Mr Ritabrata Banerjee at the same Kalighat Police Station for falsification, forging signatures of unsuspecting citizens and creation and fabrication of affidavits which have allegedly been filed before the ECI.
In the complaint filed by Mamata-Trinamool, they have also named Nanoor Police Station Officer-in-charge Sanjoy Sarkar, MLA Arup Roy, and several others as co-conspirators in the case.

“The material and evidence presently in my possession disclose that an organised exercise has been undertaken through the machinery of Nanoor Police Station for the preparation of fake affidavits in support of the rival faction, including affidavits purporting to show that ordinary members of the public recognise Arup Roy as the leader of the AITC and do not accept Smt. Mamata Banerjee as its leader,” reads the copy of the police complaint.

This comes after Mamata-AITC general secretary Abhishek Banerjee had earlier on November 5 claimed that he has video evidence of fabricated affidavits being filed out in favour of Mr. Ritabrata Banerjee.

“He says one thing in the morning, another in the evening and something else at night. Answering his questions is a waste of time and energy. I don’t have that much time,” Mr. Ritabrata Banerjee said on Monday (November 23).
West Bengal / All India Trinamool Congress / Election Commission of India

articles.title: Manik Saha says party probing presence of masked men in BJP election rally
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Tripura Chief Minister Dr. Manik Saha on Monday (November 23, 2026) reacted to the presence of several masked youths in a BJP election rally in Agartala on Saturday (November 21). He said he had come to know this from newspaper reports and subsequently took up the matter with the party leadership.
“I don’t support this. In fact, our party does not approve such behaviour from our ranks. The party is inquiring into the matter and will follow up,” he told reporters.

Elections to 21 Urban Local Bodies including Agartala Municipal Corporation (AMC) are due on November 27. The ruling BJP has already won five of them unopposed as candidates from other parties and independents did not submit nomination papers.

The appearance of several masked men at the BJP’s election rally in Agartala stirred controversy, with CPI(M) and Congress registering complaints to the state election commission. The Congress also lodged a complaint at the West Agartala Police Station.

Secretary of the State Election Commission on Monday (November 23) said they received complaints about the issues and forwarded them to the police headquarters for necessary action. He said the commission would ensure free and peaceful elections.

BJP sources said veteran minister and city campaign in-charge Ratan Lal Nath organised the procession. They said the masked youths were actually party supporters from Mohanpur, north of Agartala, home Assembly constituency of minister Nath.

CPI(M) and Congress, however, claimed the masked men were actually anti-socials who were likely to be engaged in creating trouble and rig the elections. They also complained of the silence of the police in initiating action despite registering complaints.
Tripura / Communist Party of India -Marxist / Indian National Congress / Bharatiya Janata Party

articles.title: Close to realising PM Narendra Modi’s dream for Kashmir, says Kiren Rijiju
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Terming the work of J&K Waqf Board as “the best-performing” in the country, Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs and Minority Affairs Kiren Rijiju on Monday (November 23, 2026) said the region is close to achieve the dream Prime Minister Narendra Modi has for it.

Recalling his past tours of Kashmir as Minister of State (MOS) Home and as Law Minister, Mr. Rijiju said, “I remember there were no large programmes as we visited frontier districts to meet soldiers and discuss how to realise the dream of PM Modi. I must say we are very close to realising the dream PM Modi had for Kashmir. He set a goal not only for a peaceful region but also to take J&K to new heights,” said Mr. Rijiju, while speaking at the Waqf Day-2026 at the Sher-e-Kashmir University of Agricultural Sciences and Technology in Srinagar.

Mr. Rijiju said Kashmir was moving ahead at a very “fast pace”. “Seeing the situation today, I can say India’s and J&K’s future is bright. People of Kashmir are large hearted. Today, sportsmen across the country wait to participate in the winter games at Gulmarg every year. The concept, besides adventure and water sports, was introduced in 2019,” said Mr. Rijiju.

Earlier in the day, the Union minister inaugurated the construction of Bibi Halima College of Nursing & Medical Technology (BHCNMT), at Kathi Darwaza, Rainawari, Srinagar. He said the alumni of the educational institute included 16 Kashmir University Gold Medalists, the highest among nursing colleges and over 10 international NCLEX qualifiers in the USA and Canada. “Its graduates also constitute around 30% of nursing officers at SKIMS and over 25% of the nursing workforce at Government Medical College-associated hospitals,” he added.

Praising the arrangements and management at the Nursing College and also the works done at the Hazratnal shrine, Mr. Rijiju said, “The space created at Hazratbal for female pilgrims to offer prayers is beautiful and aesthetically pleasing. I congratulate the Chairperson of the Waqf Board, Darakhshan Andrabi, in this regard. It’s the best performing board in the country.”

The Union Minister also highlighted the need to properly utilise and manage over nine lakh Waqf properties across the country. “It could bring significant socio-economic changes in the Muslim community. Poor and disadvantaged members of the Muslim community could benefit considerably if Waqf assets were utilised for their welfare, of which the J&K Waqf Board’s functioning is an example,” said Mr. Rijiju.
He also congratulated Ms. Andrabi and her entire team for “undertaking development initiatives and improving facilities at important religious and public institutions”.

Praising PM Modi for his vision. Mr. Andrabi said, “I became the first woman chairperson in 2022 and the board was constituted. There was no official structure then and the same was put in place. It is paying dividends.”

National Conference (NC) leader and Member of Parliament (MP) Mian Altaf highlighted the role of Mr. Rijiju pertaining to Kashmir. “He [Rijiju] frequently visits Kashmir and has always loved people. He always tried to contribute to Kashmir as he held different ministries. We all dream to have a better Kashmir, even what it was 30 years ago. My sister Ms. Andrabi is doing work that deserves applaud too,” said Mr. Altaf.
Jammu and Kashmir National Conference / national government / Narendra Modi
